Helping at home

My name is Rafi. I live on the third floor of a block of flats. I usually get up at seven, and I always make my bed. My sister cooks dinner on Fridays. I set the table, and after dinner I load the dishwasher. I never cook dinner alone. On Saturdays we play music with our friends. My birthday is on the twenty-first of June.

The open gate

Lena and Amir are helping at a small farm today. Lena usually feeds the ducks, but now she is looking for a lamb. Amir can see it near the garden. “We must close the gate,” he says. Their aunt comes to help them. She puts some food in a bowl, and the lamb walks towards her. The children close the gate behind it.

A windy weekend

Last weekend, Noor and her family went to a campsite near a lake. They travelled by train and arrived on Friday evening. Noor packed her camera but forgot her warm jumper. On Saturday it was windy, so they did not go sailing. They walked to a village and bought hot chocolate. Noor took photos of an old bridge. On Sunday they went home. Her favourite part was the walk.

A fruit salad for the club

Our class is making a fruit salad for the club picnic. We have got three apples, two bananas and a small bunch of grapes. We have not got any satsumas. First, we wash the fruit. Then we cut the apples and bananas into small pieces. We put the fruit in a large bowl and pour in a little orange juice. We mix it gently. We do not add any sugar.

Choosing a camp

Our club is choosing between three imaginary camps. Pine Camp costs £12 a night and is next to a lake. River Camp costs £18 a night and is beside a river. Hill Camp costs £25 a night and has the most comfortable beds. Pine Camp is the cheapest. River Camp is quieter than Hill Camp. The club chooses Pine Camp because the members want to swim in the lake and spend less money.

A Saturday plan

Maya and Leo are going to meet on Saturday. Maya has to help her grandmother in the morning, so they are going to meet at two o’clock outside the library. Leo suggests a horror film, but Maya does not like frightening stories. “Why don’t we watch the new cartoon?” she says. Leo thinks it is a good idea. They are going to walk to the cinema. They do not have to take the bus.

Lena Welcome to the Lena Andrews Show! Our guest tonight is Ricky Cooper, the actor. Ricky, you are Britain’s favourite actor.
Why do you think that is?
